definition_en: a boy or man with the same parents as you
core_image: 两个男孩并肩走在田埂上
scene: 夏天午后他们一起下河。My brother taught me to swim.
sceneCN: 这里 brother 是「兄弟」（第 1 个义项：同父母所生的男性）；句意是我哥哥教我游泳。

senses.title: A male sibling
senses.definition: a boy or man who has the same parents as you
senses.definitionCN: 与你同父母的男孩或男子
senses.example: My brother taught me to swim.
senses.exampleCN: 我哥哥教我游泳。

definition_en: having the colour of earth or wood

senses.title: A person who builds houses or structures
senses.definition: a person whose job is to build houses, walls, and other structures
senses.definitionCN: 以建造房屋、墙壁等结构为职业的人
senses.example: The builder mixed cement before laying the bricks.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑工人砌砖前先搅拌水泥。
senses.why: The agent suffix -er turns the verb build into a person who does it.
senses.whyCN: 施动者后缀 -er 把动词 build 变成「做这件事的人」，最直观的义项就是亲手施工的工人。

senses.title: A company or firm that constructs buildings
senses.definition: a business that constructs buildings, often housing estates or offices
senses.definitionCN: 承接建造业务的商业机构，常指住宅小区或办公楼开发商
senses.example: A local builder is planning a new housing estate on the edge of town.
senses.exampleCN: 一家本地营造商计划在城郊新建住宅区。
senses.why: The agent noun can be applied to organizations, not just individuals.
senses.whyCN: 施动者名词可从个人扩展到机构——「做建造这件事的主体」也可以是一家公司。

senses.title: A person who creates or develops something abstract
senses.definition: someone who develops an institution, a nation, or an idea step by step
senses.definitionCN: 逐步创建机构、国家或理念的人
senses.example: She was remembered as a builder of the modern university.
senses.exampleCN: 她被誉为这所现代大学的缔造者。
senses.why: Construction extends metaphorically from bricks to institutions.
senses.whyCN: 把「垒砖造房」的意象投射到抽象事物上，创建机构就像一砖一瓦地建设。

senses.title: In computing: a tool that assembles products from parts
senses.definition: in computing, a tool or program that assembles a product from components
senses.definitionCN: 计算机领域把组件组装成成品的工具或程序
senses.example: The website builder lets beginners create pages without code.
senses.exampleCN: 这款网站生成器让初学者无需写代码就能创建页面。
senses.why: The metaphor shifts from building physical structures to assembling digital products.
senses.whyCN: 把「组装实体结构」的隐喻搬到软件里，拼装组件生成成品的工具也叫 builder。

senses.title: A body-builder or someone who develops physique
senses.definition: used in compounds for someone who develops muscle or character
senses.definitionCN: 用于复合词，指锻炼肌肉或塑造品格的人
senses.example: He works out daily as an enthusiastic body builder.
senses.exampleCN: 他每天锻炼，是个充满热情的健美者。
senses.why: The image of building extends to shaping one's own body or character.
senses.whyCN: 「建造」的意象进一步延伸到塑造身体或品格，如 body builder（健美者）。

intro.en: Builder is the agent noun of build, formed with the Old English agent suffix -ere.
intro.cn: builder 是动词 build 的施动者名词，由古英语施动者后缀 -ere 构成，词源脉络与 build 一致。

items.en: The root of build is generally traced to a reconstructed form meaning to dwell or to cultivate, though the exact connection is uncertain.
items.cn: build 的词根一般认为可追溯到一个表示「居住；耕作」的重构形式 *bhu-, 具体演变链条存疑。

items.en: The verb build (bilden, byldan) meant to construct a house, and the agent suffix -ere already existed.
items.cn: 古英语动词 bildan 义为「建造房屋」，同时已有施动者后缀 -ere（表示「做某事的人」）。

items.en: The noun builder appears in Middle English around the 14th-15th century, meaning one who constructs.
items.cn: 中古英语时期（约 14 至 15 世纪）出现 builder，义为「建造者」。

items.en: The meaning expanded from individual craftsmen to firms that organize construction work.
items.cn: 近代英语时期，词义从个体工匠扩展到组织施工的商业机构（营造商）。

items.en: The word now covers builders of nations and software, a productive metaphor.
items.cn: 现代英语中 builder 也指国家建设者和软件构建工具，隐喻用法活跃。

note.en: Words that share the build root or look similar, and near concepts in the same field.
note.cn: 本组区分与 build 同根的词、拼写相近的词，以及建筑领域内的近义概念。

definition_en: to hit something lightly and suddenly
core_image: 车轮压过石头时车身一颠

senses.title: To hit something lightly
senses.definition: to hit something by accident, usually not hard
senses.definitionCN: 意外地、通常不重地撞到某物
senses.example: She bumped her knee on the table.
senses.exampleCN: 她的膝盖撞到了桌子。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, naming a dull knock.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，指一声闷响的撞击。

senses.title: To move with jolts

entries.definition: the bright burning gas of a fire

normalIntro.en: Burn is heat doing damage or giving warmth.
normalIntro.cn: burn 就是热在起作用，或带来温暖，或造成损伤。

normal.en: Dry wood burns quickly.
The past participle is burnt in British use.
normal.cn: 英式用法中过去分词常作 burnt。

normal.en: A burner is the part that makes flame.
normal.cn: burner 是产生火焰的部件。

normal.en: You burn a disc with a laser.
To burn with anger is to be furious.
normal.cn: burn with anger 指怒火中烧。

abstract.en: See orange flames behind a stove door.
abstract.cn: 想象炉门后跳动的橘色火。

abstract.en: See a red mark rising on a palm.
abstract.cn: 想象手心浮起一道红痕。

abstract.en: See a thin bright line cut into a disc.
abstract.cn: 想象盘面被刻出细细的亮痕。

examples.en: The fire burned slowly in the stove.
examples.cn: 炉火在炉膛里慢慢烧着。

examples.en: He burned his hand on the pan.
examples.cn: 他的手被锅烫伤了。

examples.en: She burned the photos onto a disc.
examples.cn: 她把照片刻录到光盘上。

dict_mnemonic.text: burn 与 born 只差一个字母，火能烧毁东西，也能让新的东西从灰里生出来。

root: burn 源自古英语 beornan，本义为「正在燃烧」，中古英语起兼指点火与烧毁，十四世纪起作名词指烫伤，二十世纪又用于激光「刻录」光盘。

sensesIntro.en: Fire giving heat, heat hurting skin, and a laser writing data.
sensesIntro.cn: 放出热量的火、灼伤皮肤的热、以及激光写入数据。

intro.cn: burn 加 -er 与 -able 可表示部件与性质。

definition_en: to break open suddenly
core_image: 冻裂的水管喷出一束水
scene: 天太冷，屋里忽然传来一声闷响。The pipe burst under the floor.
sceneCN: 这里 burst 是「爆裂」（第 1 个义项：因内部压力突然裂开）；句意是地板下的水管爆裂了。

senses.title: To break open suddenly
senses.definition: to break open because of pressure inside
senses.definitionCN: 因内部压力而突然裂开
senses.example: The pipe burst under the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 地板下的水管爆裂了。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, naming something splitting from within.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，指从内部裂开。

senses.title: To happen or appear suddenly
senses.definition: to begin suddenly and strongly, as tears or laughter
senses.definitionCN: 眼泪、笑声等突然而强烈地出现
senses.example: She burst into tears at the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到这个消息她突然大哭起来。
senses.why: Feeling held inside escapes the way water escapes a cracked pipe.
senses.whyCN: 憋在里面的情绪冲出来，正如水冲出裂管。

senses.title: A short sudden outbreak
senses.definition: a short sudden period of activity or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 短暂而突然的一阵动作或情绪
senses.example: A burst of applause filled the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵掌声充满大厅。
senses.why: The noun names the moment of breaking out.
senses.whyCN: 名词指「冲出来」的那一瞬间。

intro.en: Burst is an old word for breaking open from within.
intro.cn: burst 是表示「从内部炸开」的老词。

items.en: berstan meant to break or split suddenly.
items.cn: berstan 意为突然破裂。

items.en: burst kept the sense of violent splitting.
items.cn: burst 保留猛烈裂开的义项。

items.en: Burst into tears described feeling breaking out.
items.cn: burst into tears 形容情绪冲出。

items.en: The noun named a short outbreak of sound.
items.cn: 名词指声音的一阵爆发。

normalIntro.en: Burst is pressure finding a way out.
normalIntro.cn: burst 就是压力找到了出口。

normal.en: A burst pipe floods the floor.
normal.cn: 爆裂的水管会淹了地板。

normal.en: The past tense stays burst.
An outburst is a sudden rush of feeling.
She burst into tears at the news.
A burst of speed wins the last metre.
normal.cn: 最后一段靠一股冲刺的劲。
